salaryRaise.title: Salary Raise Calculator
salaryRaise.subtitle: Convert between raise rate, new salary and raise amount, then see how much your monthly take-home pay really grows and what the raise is worth after inflation.

input.title: Salary details
input.valueErr: Keep the new salary between ₩1M and ₩1B and the rate between -50% and 100%
input.nonTaxableHint: Meal allowance is tax-free up to ₩200,000 a month. Tax-free pay has no tax or social insurance.
input.dependentsHint: The family count used in the withholding tax table. Enter 1 if it is only you.
input.yearHint: Employee share: pension {pension} · health {health} · long-term care {ltc} of health premium · employment {emp}

result.sameYear: Before and after both use {year} rates, {dep} dependent(s) and a ₩{nt} monthly tax-free allowance.

inflation.title: What the raise is worth after inflation
inflation.customHint: You can type your own. Forecasts are from the Bank of Korea (Aug 2026), actuals from Statistics Korea.
inflation.negative: The raise is below {cpi}% inflation, so your purchasing power goes down.

offer.title: Compare with a job offer
offer.desc: Compare your current employer's raise with another company's offer in monthly take-home pay.
offer.label: Offered salary
offer.hint: Uses the same dependents and tax-free allowance.
offer.example: Leave it empty to compare with an example of 110% of your salary (₩{v}).
offer.same: Both give the same monthly take-home pay.
offer.more: The offer pays ₩{diff} more per month after tax (₩{annual} difference in salary).
offer.less: Staying pays ₩{diff} more per month after tax (₩{annual} difference in salary).
offer.note: Besides salary, compare bonus rules, retirement pension type (DB or DC), tax-free allowances, benefits and commuting time. At a new company, annual leave restarts at the under-one-year rate (1 day per month of full attendance).

formula.title: Formulas
items: Raise rate (%) = (new salary − current salary) ÷ current salary × 100. Going from ₩50M to ₩52.5M is 5%.
New salary = current salary × (1 + raise rate). The monthly raise (pre-tax) is the annual raise divided by 12.

Monthly take-home pay is calculated the same way as Toolhub's salary calculator: minus the employee share of social insurance, income tax from the withholding tax table and local income tax (10% of income tax).
Real raise = (1 + raise rate) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1. A 5% raise with 2.7% inflation is about 2.24%.

why.title: Why take-home pay rises less
items: Income tax is progressive, from 6% to 45% by bracket. The added salary is taxed at a higher rate than your current average.
The employee share of social insurance is proportional to taxable pay. With 2027 rates it adds up to about 10% of taxable pay.
National pension has a monthly earnings cap (₩6.59M from Jul 2026 to Jun 2027), so very high salaries pay no extra pension on the raise.
Tax-free allowances such as meals carry no tax or social insurance, so the same raise paid as a tax-free item increases take-home pay more.
Monthly income tax follows the withholding table. Your final tax is settled in the year-end tax settlement based on your deductions.

tips.title: Negotiation tips
items: Anchor on official data: wages grew 3.1% in 2025 (Ministry of Employment and Labor) and the Bank of Korea expects 2.7% inflation in 2026. That supports asking for at least an inflation-matching raise.
Pay levels by industry, company size and occupation are available on the Ministry of Employment and Labor's wage portal (wagework.go.kr).
Check the monthly take-home increase with this calculator, not just the pre-tax rate, to avoid surprises.
Compare total compensation: salary plus bonuses, tax-free allowances, retirement pension and benefits.
Get the agreed salary in a written employment or salary contract. Article 17 of the Labor Standards Act requires the pay components, calculation and payment method to be stated in writing.
If your pay is close to the minimum wage, make sure it is not below the 2027 minimum wage (₩10,700 an hour, ₩2,236,300 for 209 hours a month).

items.q: How much does take-home pay grow with a 5% raise?
items.a: For a ₩50M salary (₩200,000 monthly meal allowance, 1 dependent, 2027 rates), monthly take-home pay goes from about ₩3.56M to about ₩3.72M, roughly ₩158,000 more. About 24% of the ₩2.5M annual raise goes to income tax and social insurance, so take-home pay rises about 4.4%.

items.q: How is the raise rate calculated?
items.a: (new salary − current salary) ÷ current salary × 100. From ₩42M to ₩45M is ₩3M ÷ ₩42M × 100, about 7.14%. Enter any one of rate, new salary or amount and the calculator converts the others.

items.q: Why doesn't take-home pay rise as much as my salary?
items.a: Income tax is progressive, so the added salary is taxed above your current average rate, and social insurance applies to the added pay too. Take-home pay therefore usually rises a little less than the headline rate.

items.q: How do I read the real raise after inflation?
items.a: It is (1 + raise rate) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1. The Bank of Korea (Aug 2026) forecasts consumer prices to rise 2.7% in 2026 and 2.3% in 2027; actual 2025 inflation was 2.1% (Statistics Korea). If your raise is below inflation, your real income falls.

items.q: What is the average salary increase?
items.a: In the Ministry of Employment and Labor's establishment survey, nominal wages per worker rose 3.1% in 2025 and real wages rose 0.9%. It varies widely by company size, industry and performance, so use it as a reference.

items.q: How should I compare a job offer?
items.a: Enter the amount in 'Compare with a job offer' to see the monthly take-home difference against your current raise. Also weigh bonuses, retirement pension, tax-free allowances, benefits and commuting time.

In 2027 the employee pension share rises from 4.75% to 5% and long-term care rises from 13.14% to 13.9% of the health premium, so the same salary takes home slightly less. The proposed employment insurance increase (0.9% to 1.0%) is not yet in the enforcement decree, so 0.9% is used.
